transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. I feel like how I look and what I weigh is the only thing that matters about me now, and it’s starting to take over my life around food. It has just become really exhausting to deal with every single day.
Do you find yourself engaging in episodes where you eat a very large amount of food in a short time, and do you feel a loss of control during those moments?

Yes, on bad nights, it feels like a switch flips and I'll secretly tear through a massive amount of food—like half a loaf of bread, leftovers, and chips—in under an hour. Even while I'm telling myself to stop, my hands just keep going and I feel completely unable to control it. I only end up stopping when I'm uncomfortably full and starting to feel sick.

After these episodes of eating a large amount of food, do you ever feel the need to engage in behaviors to prevent weight gain, such as self-induced vomiting, excessive exercise, or the misuse of laxatives?

Yes, I usually end up in the bathroom forcing myself to throw up until I taste acid, trying to "undo the damage" so I don't wake up heavier the next day. I'll also skip meals to make up for it, and this pattern of binging and then purging or fasting happens at least a couple of times every week.
